- logging.py: defer Traceback to emit() (only when rich_tracebacks=True)
- logging.py: use future annotations + TYPE_CHECKING for Console,
  ConsoleRenderable, Highlighter, FormatTimeCallable (annotation-only)
- logging.py: replace pathlib.Path with os.path.basename
- console.py: eliminate import inspect (~10ms); replace isclass with
  isinstance(x, type), currentframe with sys._getframe
- console.py: defer pretty to Console.print()
- console.py: defer scope to Console.log() (only when log_locals=True)
- console.py: defer getpass to Console.input() (only when password=True)
- console.py: defer html.escape and zlib to export methods
- segment.py: remove dead logging import (getLogger never used)
- theme.py: defer configparser to Theme.from_file()

Combined effect (Standard_D2s_v5, CPython 3.13, hyperfine):
  Console import: 78.8ms → 52.0ms (1.52x faster)

<p dir="auto">
Rich is a Python library for 
<em>rich</em>
 text and beautiful formatting in the terminal.
</p>
<p dir="auto">
The 
<a href="https://rich.readthedocs.io/en/latest/" rel="nofollow">Rich API</a>
 makes it easy to add color and style to terminal output. Rich can also render pretty tables, progress bars, markdown, syntax highlighted source code, tracebacks, and more — out of the box.
</p>
<p dir="auto">
<a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="https://github.com/textualize/rich/raw/main/imgs/features.png">

</a>
</p>

As you might expect, this will print 
<code>"Hello World!"</code>
 to the terminal. Note that unlike the builtin 
<code>print</code>
 function, Rich will word-wrap your text to fit within the terminal width.
</p>
<p dir="auto">
There are a few ways of adding color and style to your output. You can set a style for the entire output by adding a 
<code>style</code>
 keyword argument. Here's an example:
</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto">
<pre><span class="pl-s1">console</span>
.
<span class="pl-c1">print</span>
(
<span class="pl-s">"Hello"</span>
, 
<span class="pl-s">"World!"</span>
, 
<span class="pl-s1">style</span>
<span class="pl-c1">=</span>
<span class="pl-s">"bold red"</span>
)
</pre>

<p dir="auto">
Rich contains a number of builtin 
<em>renderables</em>
 you can use to create elegant output in your CLI and help you debug your code.
</p>
<p dir="auto">Click the following headings for details:</p>
<details>
<summary>
Log
</summary>
<p dir="auto">
The Console object has a 
<code>log()</code>
 method which has a similar interface to 
<code>print()</code>
, but also renders a column for the current time and the file and line which made the call. By default Rich will do syntax highlighting for Python structures and for repr strings. If you log a collection (i.e. a dict or a list) Rich will pretty print it so that it fits in the available space. Here's an example of some of these features.
</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto">
<pre><span class="pl-k">from</span> <span class="pl-s1">rich</span>
.
<span class="pl-s1">console</span> <span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-v">Console</span>
<span class="pl-s1">console</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-en">Console</span>
()


<span class="pl-s1">test_data</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span>
 [
    {
<span class="pl-s">"jsonrpc"</span>
: 
<span class="pl-s">"2.0"</span>
, 
<span class="pl-s">"method"</span>
: 
<span class="pl-s">"sum"</span>
, 
<span class="pl-s">"params"</span>
: [
<span class="pl-c1">None</span>
, 
<span class="pl-c1">1</span>
, 
<span class="pl-c1">2</span>
, 
<span class="pl-c1">4</span>
, 
<span class="pl-c1">False</span>
, 
<span class="pl-c1">True</span>
], 
<span class="pl-s">"id"</span>
: 
<span class="pl-s">"1"</span>
,},
    {
<span class="pl-s">"jsonrpc"</span>
: 
<span class="pl-s">"2.0"</span>
, 
<span class="pl-s">"method"</span>
: 
<span class="pl-s">"notify_hello"</span>
, 
<span class="pl-s">"params"</span>
: [
<span class="pl-c1">7</span>
]},
    {
<span class="pl-s">"jsonrpc"</span>
: 
<span class="pl-s">"2.0"</span>
, 
<span class="pl-s">"method"</span>
: 
<span class="pl-s">"subtract"</span>
, 
<span class="pl-s">"params"</span>
: [
<span class="pl-c1">42</span>
, 
<span class="pl-c1">23</span>
], 
<span class="pl-s">"id"</span>
: 
<span class="pl-s">"2"</span>
},
]


<span class="pl-k">def</span> <span class="pl-en">test_log</span>
():
    
<span class="pl-s1">enabled</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-c1">False</span>
    <span class="pl-s1">context</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span>
 {
        
<span class="pl-s">"foo"</span>
: 
<span class="pl-s">"bar"</span>
,
    }
    
<span class="pl-s1">movies</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span>
 [
<span class="pl-s">"Deadpool"</span>
, 
<span class="pl-s">"Rise of the Skywalker"</span>
]
    
<span class="pl-s1">console</span>
.
<span class="pl-c1">log</span>
(
<span class="pl-s">"Hello from"</span>
, 
<span class="pl-s1">console</span>
, 
<span class="pl-s">"!"</span>
)
    
<span class="pl-s1">console</span>
.
<span class="pl-c1">log</span>
(
<span class="pl-s1">test_data</span>
, 
<span class="pl-s1">log_locals</span>
<span class="pl-c1">=</span>
<span class="pl-c1">True</span>
)



<span class="pl-en">test_log</span>
()
</pre>

For basic usage, wrap any sequence in the 
<code>track</code>

<span class="pl-s1">progress</span> <span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-s1">track</span>

<span class="pl-k">for</span> <span class="pl-s1">step</span> <span class="pl-c1">in</span> <span class="pl-en">track</span>
(
<span class="pl-en">range</span>
(
<span class="pl-c1">100</span>
)):
    
<span class="pl-en">do_step</span>
(
<span class="pl-s1">step</span>
)
</pre>

<details>
<summary>
Status
</summary>
<p dir="auto">
For situations where it is hard to calculate progress, you can use the 
<a href="https://rich.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/console.html#rich.console.Console.status" rel="nofollow">status</a>
 method which will display a 'spinner' animation and message. The animation won't prevent you from using the console as normal. Here's an example:
</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto">
<pre><span class="pl-k">from</span> <span class="pl-s1">time</span> <span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-s1">sleep</span>
<span class="pl-k">from</span> <span class="pl-s1">rich</span>
.
<span class="pl-s1">console</span> <span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-v">Console</span>

<span class="pl-s1">console</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-en">Console</span>
()

<span class="pl-s1">tasks</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span>
 [
<span class="pl-s">
f"task 
<span class="pl-s1">
<span class="pl-kos">{</span>
<span class="pl-s1">n</span>
<span class="pl-kos">}</span>
</span>
"
</span> <span class="pl-k">for</span> <span class="pl-s1">n</span> <span class="pl-c1">in</span> <span class="pl-en">range</span>
(
<span class="pl-c1">1</span>
, 
<span class="pl-c1">11</span>
)]


<span class="pl-k">with</span> <span class="pl-s1">console</span>
.
<span class="pl-c1">status</span>
(
<span class="pl-s">"[bold green]Working on tasks..."</span>
) 
<span class="pl-k">as</span> <span class="pl-s1">status</span>
:
    
<span class="pl-k">while</span> <span class="pl-s1">tasks</span>
:
        
<span class="pl-s1">task</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">tasks</span>
.
<span class="pl-c1">pop</span>
(
<span class="pl-c1">0</span>
)
        
<span class="pl-en">sleep</span>
(
<span class="pl-c1">1</span>
)
        
<span class="pl-s1">console</span>
.
<span class="pl-c1">log</span>
(
<span class="pl-s">
f"
<span class="pl-s1">
<span class="pl-kos">{</span>
<span class="pl-s1">task</span>
<span class="pl-kos">}</span>
</span>
 complete"
</span>
)
</pre>
<div class="zeroclipboard-container">
    <clipboard-copy aria-label="Copy code to clipboard" class="ClipboardButton btn btn-invisible js-clipboard-copy m-2 p-0 d-flex flex-justify-center flex-items-center" data-copy-feedback="Copied!" data-tooltip-direction="w" value="from time import sleep
from rich.console import Console

console = Console()
tasks = [f"task {n}" for n in range(1, 11)]

with console.status("[bold green]Working on tasks...") as status:
    while tasks:
        task = tasks.pop(0)
        sleep(1)
        console.log(f"{task} complete")" tabindex="0" role="button">

Syntax Highlighting
</summary>
<p dir="auto">
Rich uses the 
<a href="https://pygments.org/" rel="nofollow">pygments</a>
 library to implement 
<a href="https://rich.readthedocs.io/en/latest/syntax.html" rel="nofollow">syntax highlighting</a>
. Usage is similar to rendering markdown; construct a 
<code>Syntax</code>
 object and print it to the console. Here's an example:
</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto">
<pre><span class="pl-k">from</span> <span class="pl-s1">rich</span>
.
<span class="pl-s1">console</span> <span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-v">Console</span>
<span class="pl-k">from</span> <span class="pl-s1">rich</span>
.
<span class="pl-s1">syntax</span> <span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-v">Syntax</span>

<span class="pl-s1">my_code</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s">'''</span>
<span class="pl-s">def iter_first_last(values: Iterable[T]) -> Iterable[Tuple[bool, bool, T]]:</span>
<span class="pl-s">    """Iterate and generate a tuple with a flag for first and last value."""</span>
<span class="pl-s">    iter_values = iter(values)</span>
<span class="pl-s">    try:</span>
<span class="pl-s">        previous_value = next(iter_values)</span>
<span class="pl-s">    except StopIteration:</span>
<span class="pl-s">        return</span>
<span class="pl-s">    first = True</span>
<span class="pl-s">    for value in iter_values:</span>
<span class="pl-s">        yield first, False, previous_value</span>
